title: Control the specified trapping clock with a boundary-corrected Foster function
statement: For R={0<->A+B,B<->2B},activitiesa,b and equal pair circulations, the accepted rates are cF_K(A+B),cAB/(ab)F_K(A+B-2),cB/b F_K(A+B-1),cB(B-1)/b^2 F_K(A+B-2). Let beta=2+2a/b and H=(A-B)^2+beta B^2+(beta+a)1_{B=0}. At B=0 only birth changes population and DeltaH=-a. At B=1 the exact nominal drift/c is3beta F_K(A+1)+(A/b)F_K(A-1)+(-2A+3+3beta)F_K(A)/b, with strictly negative large-A margin surviving independent errors<=1/4. For B>=2, the explicit grouped negative AB^2 and B^3 terms dominate the positive lower-order terms outside a polynomial activity-controlled region, with the stated robust margins. For accepted K>=2, powers(1+H)^s have computable polynomial-V Foster bounds; H compares to(A+B)^2 up to polynomial activity factors. Hence sufficient stationary/transient moments hold and channel-coupling transfer gives the complete robust contract for THIS interacting infinite-class network. Its jump-chain gap can still be zero. The visible producer Sympy identity check is preserved, not rerun or treated as an all-error validation.

Conditional transfer assumes, rather than proves generally, perturbed nonexplosion/positive recurrence/unique stationary law and sufficient uniform polynomial moments, including nominal evolution started from perturbed stationary laws. No novelty, physical device advantage or independent validation is claimed; all held/unread sources and transfer limits persist. This is numerical population/activity/accuracy cost, not polynomial physical cost in logarithmic population. Use accepted nominal exact-law/gap constants once.
